metadata.content: Mary Earps exclusive: London City Lionesses goalkeeper on busy summer transfer window and facing Man Utd in WSL opener | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Mary Earps exclusive: London City Lionesses goalkeeper on busy summer transfer window and facing Man Utd in WSL opener Mary Earps joined London City Lionesses this summer and was followed by the likes of Alexia Putellas, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani; watch London City Lionesses vs Man Utd on the opening weekend of the WSL season on September 4, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 7pm Charlotte Marsh Senior Football Journalist Monday 31 August 2026 12:27, UK Image: Mary Earps has signed for London City Lionesses this summer from PSG - just one of their superstar additions Mary Earps is used to leading from the front, whether as an England goalkeeper or highlighting issues in the women's game. This summer, she was the first one through the door as London City Lionesses collated a star-strewn squad. The goalkeeper returns to the WSL after a two-year spell in France with PSG, something she describes as 'a very different environment'. Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports ahead of the WSL's return on September 4, when London City face her former side, Manchester United, Earps said: "I really feel like I was able to go away and work on myself for a couple of years. messages.text: England's batting conundrum: Who misses out when Bethell returns?

metadata.summary: Like a finalist on TV game show Countdown, England are going to have to deal with a particularly tricky conundrum.
metadata.content: England's Test batting conundrum: Will Jordan Cox, Dan Lawrence or Emilio Gay miss out when Jacob Bethell is fit again? | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis England's Test batting conundrum: Will Jordan Cox, Dan Lawrence or Emilio Gay miss out when Jacob Bethell is fit again? England will have big decision to make in South Africa this winter when Jacob Bethell is fit again after a knee injury; Jordan Cox has impressed against Pakistan in Bethell's absence and staked claim for longer run in the side, perhaps putting pressure on opener Emilio Gay Monday 31 August 2026 13:30, UK Image: England face a batting conundrum in their Test side when Jacob Bethell returns to fitness after a knee injury Like a finalist on TV game show Countdown, England are going to have to deal with a particularly tricky conundrum. Ben Stokes' international retirement and Jacob Bethell's knee injury offered opportunities to Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence in the Test match batting line-up and those have largely been seized, albeit against a struggling Pakistan side. While we don't think Stokes is going to make a comeback - although don't entirely rule it out - Bethell is set to return for the three-Test series in South Africa over the winter, leaving England with one batter too many for their XI. metadata.summary: Ripon’s Champion Two Years Old Trophy is up for grabs on Bank Holiday Monday, plus action from Chepstow and Southwell, all live on Sky Sports Racing.
metadata.content: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Two-year-old Trophy up for grabs at Ripon | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Today on Sky Sports Racing: Two-year-old Trophy up for grabs at Ripon Clash Of Hearts and Rogue Jewel feature in Monday's Champion Two Years Old Trophy at Ripon; Simon & Ed Crisford looking for fourth win in race in last seven years with Pure Mint; watch every race live on Sky Sports Racing Saturday 29 August 2026 16:22, UK Image: Bank Holiday Monday racing comes from Ripon, Chepstow & Southwell Ripon’s Champion Two Years Old Trophy is up for grabs on Bank Holiday Monday, plus action from Chepstow and Southwell, all live on Sky Sports Racing. 3.05 Ripon - Clash Of Hearts has leading claims Clash Of Hearts comes here with the form in the bank after bringing up his first win at Pontefract in empathic fashion. He then ran a credible race at Glorious Goodwood in a nursery and most recently was fifth in the Group Three Acomb Stakes at York where he was just over five lengths behind the well-fancied winner, Haffner. Rogue Jewel is two from two for The Rogues Gallery team and brings course and distance form to the race as he bought up his second win here at the track just recently. He looks promising for Ed Bethell. Impressive scorer Pure Mint represents Simon & Ed Crisford under Harry Davies after bolting up here last month. The Crisfords pose a strong record here having taken out three of the last six renewals and they should be respected here with this son of Minzaal.
